definitions.explanation: The place on a riverbank or shore where a ferry boat takes on and lets off passengers. Common in descriptions of pre-modern travel, before bridges were built.

examples.japanese: {渡|わた}し{場|ば}で{船|ふね}を{待|ま}つ。
examples.english: To wait for the boat at the ferry landing.

examples.japanese: {昔|むかし}、この{川|かわ}には{渡|わた}し{場|ば}があった。
examples.english: Long ago there was a ferry crossing on this river.

examples.japanese: {橋|はし}ができる{前|まえ}は、{村|むら}の{人|ひと}たちは{渡|わた}し{場|ば}から{舟|ふね}に{乗|の}って{対岸|たいがん}へ{渡|わた}っていた。
examples.english: Before the bridge was built, the villagers boarded boats at the ferry landing and crossed to the far bank.

notes:
From {渡|わた}す (to carry across) + {場|ば} (place). Many Japanese place names preserve old crossings, and the word appears frequently in historical fiction and local history.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {渡|わた}し{場|ば}に{着|つ}く: to reach the ferry landing
- {渡|わた}し{場|ば}の{跡|あと}: the site of a former ferry crossing
- {渡|わた}し{船|ぶね}: a ferry boat

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {船着|ふなつ}き{場|ば}: boat landing, dock — any place boats tie up, not necessarily a crossing
- {港|みなと}: harbor, port — much larger, for shipping rather than a short crossing
